question: A collector had 52 items. They subtracted 35 for a sale. They subtracted 1 more for a return. They multiplied by 8 for batch counting. They multiplied by 5 for regional projection. They multiplied by 6 for expansion planning. An auction house had 1000 items but wasn't involved. After the two subtractions, before the first multiplication, how many?

A traveler had 41 dollars initially. They spent 5 on transit (morning). They added 15 from finding money (afternoon). They spent 48 on meals. They spent 2 more on tips. They added 26 from a refund (evening). Time was measured in hours for tracking (unit change). They had a credit card with 200 available but didn't use it. After morning and afternoon but before meal spending—how much?

A student had 30 dollars initially. They subtracted 12 for textbooks (morning). They subtracted 8 more for supplies (afternoon). They added 43 from a job (evening). They multiplied by 4 for savings projection. They added 4 dollars. Their monthly budget was 200 dollars. After the two morning/afternoon subtractions but before the addition, how much?

A warehouse started with 228 units. They added 40 units. They subtracted 27 units. They added 65 more units. They added 66 units. They divided by half for inventory counting. A competing warehouse held 500 units. After all additions and subtraction but before division—with two named people comparing: Manager A had this count while Manager B had half—how many total?

A factory started with 38 items hourly. They multiplied by 4 through efficiency. They multiplied by 8 through shifts. They multiplied by 7 through automation. They multiplied by 4 through scaling. They multiplied by 5 for projections (unit measured in hours for production). They subtracted 17781 after inventory. A competitor made 50000 items yearly separately. After all multiplications but before subtracting the large batch, what was produced?

A business started with 101 dollars. They multiplied by 9 through growth. They added 58 dollars. They added 23 dollars from sales. They added 65 more from deals. They subtracted 776 for expenses. A loan of 1000 dollars was available but unused. After multiplication but before adding the first sales amount, how much did they have?

A library started with 213 books. They tripled the collection (multiplied by 3). They subtracted 549 for archiving. They multiplied by 7 for facility projections. They added 12 newly catalogued books. A donation of 100 books came later separately. Using a word quantity—triple the original amount—how many books after multiplying but before archiving?

A school had 69 students. They multiplied by 8 through enrollment growth. They multiplied by 6 through expanded sections (morning activity). They divided by 4 for classroom grouping. They added 56 transfer students (afternoon update). They multiplied by 6 more for facility planning. They divided by 4 for final scheduling. Two principals managed 30 students each separately. After morning and afternoon activities but before evening division, how many students?

A store started with 236 items. They subtracted 90 for sales. They added 17 from restocking. They subtracted 64 more for another sale. They added 40 from a delivery. Maria had 200 items at her store but unrelated. After initial sales and restocking but before the second sale, how many items remained?

A player had 165 points. They subtracted 63 through enemy damage. They added 78 from bonuses. They subtracted 166 from another challenge. They multiplied by 6 for final scoring. Tom had 500 points in a different game. After subtracting both damage amounts but before multiplication, how many points?

A student started with 175 dollars. They subtracted 122 for textbooks (morning). They subtracted 1 more for taxes (afternoon, using a word quantity like 'half'). They multiplied by 7 for scholarship projection. They multiplied by 6 for total aid calculation. They added 71 dollars. A tuition cost was 5000 dollars separately. After the two subtractions but before multiplication, how much in the account (in an afternoon snapshot)?

A business started with 235 dollars. They multiplied by 5 for growth projection. They divided by 5 (returning to original). They subtracted 138 for overhead. They subtracted 90 more for supplies. They multiplied by 2 for future value. A competitor's budget was 1000 dollars separately. After multiplication/division and first subtraction but before the second subtraction, using a unit change (dollars to cents), how much?

A student had 44 hours available. They doubled it (multiplied by 2, morning). They added 71 more hours of study time (afternoon). They subtracted 14 for breaks. They multiplied by 6 for semester planning. They divided by 3 for weekly breakdown. A full year had 52 weeks separately. After doubling and adding but before subtracting breaks, how many hours in the afternoon?

A town had 19 parks. They added 68 through new construction. They added 36 more. They multiplied by 9 for master planning. They added 70 final parks. A nearby city had 500 parks but unrelated. After both additions but before the multiplication, how many parks did the town have?

A collector had 148 cards. They multiplied by 6 through purchasing (morning). They multiplied by 2 through trading (afternoon). They multiplied by 2 through another round. They multiplied by 9 for bulk inventory. Alex had 1000 cards but wasn't counted. Sarah had 500 cards also separate. After morning and afternoon activities but before the second afternoon round, how many cards after each of the first two multiplications?

A gardener started with 121 seeds. They doubled the batch (multiplied by 2). They added 18 more seeds. They multiplied by 7 for harvest projection. They subtracted 428 seeds used in planting. The plot size was 200 square feet but didn't affect seed count. After doubling and adding but before the larger multiplication, how many seeds?

A baker had 61 loaves. They subtracted 35 (morning sale). They doubled remaining (multiplied by 2). They multiplied by 6 for a catering order. They divided by half for packaging. They added 69 loaves (afternoon restock). They added 62 more (evening). A competitor made 300 loaves separately. After morning sale and doubling but before catering multiplication, how many loaves?

An athlete had 95 kilometers to train. They multiplied by 7 through sprint intervals. They subtracted 108 for recovery days. They multiplied by 7 for weekly totals. They subtracted 1132 for major rest. They subtracted 958 more for facility maintenance time. Using 'half' as a word quantity, a coach's regimen was 50 kilometers separately. After sprints but before recovery subtraction, how many kilometers?

A factory had 196 items. They tripled (multiplied by 3). They divided by 6 for packaging. They multiplied by 3 more for batch scaling. They multiplied by 7 for production runs. They multiplied by 9 for annual projection. A competitor produced 5000 items, using 'double' as a word quantity. After tripling but before the division, how many items?

A student had 30 minutes. They subtracted 2 for setup (morning). They added 57 for extension (afternoon). They subtracted 28 for lunch. They divided by 3 for group work. They added 45 more minutes (evening). The school day lasted 360 minutes but this was separate. After all morning and afternoon activities but before the evening division, how much time in minutes?

A student had 171 pages to read. They subtracted 12 for skipped sections (morning). They added 41 (afternoon). They multiplied by 9 for related readings. They multiplied by 6 for semester material. Lisa had 500 pages assigned but different. After subtracting and adding morning material but before multiplication, how many pages to cover?

A warehouse had 204 boxes. They added 43 (morning). They added 5 more (afternoon). They multiplied by 4 for batch stacking. They multiplied by 4 more for shipping. Tom's warehouse had 500 boxes but separate. After both morning and afternoon additions but before stacking multiplication, how many boxes total?

A collector had 135 items. They added 28 new items (morning). They subtracted 140 for donations (afternoon). They added 15 back from returns. They subtracted 29 for trades. Using 'half' as a word quantity—the donations were half his original. After morning addition and afternoon donation but before the return, how many items?

A library had 158 books. They added 48 (morning). They subtracted 86 for binding (mid-morning). They subtracted 117 more for archiving (afternoon). They divided by 3 for classification (evening). Using 'half' as a word quantity and showing time progression—the books represented half the collection originally. After additions and subtractions but before division, how many books?

A student had 158 study materials. They multiplied by 7 through compilation. They subtracted 1090 for redistribution (and used a word quantity like 'double'). They multiplied by 9 more for semester projection. They multiplied by 2 for annual planning. Tom and Sarah studied together (named comparison), measuring study-hours as a unit change. After multiplication but before the large subtraction, how many materials?
